title: M4 MacBook Air 16GB/512GB for Local LLMs and agent based trading- worth $800?
author: soboinsomniac
selftext:
Planning to buy a MacBook Air M4 (16 GB / 512 GB) for about $800 to run local LLM agents for:

Indian mid‑cap equity research (using Screener.in CSVs)

Building/testing trading ideas via Zerodha Kite API (prices, history, holdings; maybe orders later)

Also want to run Hermes-based agents on it

Questions:

On 16 GB M4 Air, which local LLMs are best for reasoning, coding, and tool use? Is Qwen 3.5 9B (Q4) + a smaller fast model (e.g. LFM2.5 8B / Llama 3.2 3B) a good combo alongside Hermes?

Best local stack (Ollama vs LM Studio, etc.) and any existing Kite + LLM or Indian‑stock agent projects to reference?

Any tips on context length, thermals, and multi‑agent setups (including Hermes) on a 16 GB fanless Air?

Getting the laptop for \~$800, so stuck with 16 GB for now. If you’ve done similar work (local LLMs for equity research / algo trading, especially in India), what models and setup would you recommend?

Thanks!

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
16gb is the constraint and it bites on the multi agent part specifically. a 9B at Q4 plus its context plus whatever the OS and a browser are sitting on leaves very little room, and the two model combo you describe means either keeping both resident or eating a load and unload on every handoff. one model at a time is comfortable on that machine. a fleet of agents is not.

the other thing worth saying is that for screener CSVs and Kite history the model is not your bottleneck, the data plumbing is. i would spend the first month getting clean bars and a fetch that does not silently skip days, and only then argue about which local model reads them. you can swap the model in an afternoon. you cannot swap a broken data layer.

replies.author: soboinsomniac
replies.body:
Noted , thank you . 

Was tempted by the " deal " price and I am going to be dipping my toes so did not want to go all in for a expensive mac ,

This is going to be a secondary device to run only for doing trades

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: A dedicated second machine is a different calculation. 16gb bites when a browser, Slack and the model are all fighting for it. A box that only runs the stack has most of that back. I'd keep the broker connection on something you don't reboot for experiments, though.

comments.author: akai0102
comments.body: 16g just can go with llm api, at least 32g for single local llm.

replies.author: soboinsomniac
replies.body: Thats the back up option, but not sure about giving my broker log in and other details, thus the want to run it locally

comments.author: Electrical_Lie2336
comments.body: For equity research, I’d optimize the local setup for reproducibility rather than just model size: keep a compact brief with the sources, assumptions, bull/bear cases, and a risk matrix, then verify the numbers in the filings before any trade. That makes it easier to spot when an agent is confidently wrong.

comments.author: BatteryAlmostFull
comments.body: I have mabook air m5 and an alienware x15 with rtx3070, for local llm RTX is the best, but macbook m5 is nice to use cause is quiet

comments.author: InevitableAd9080
comments.body: do yourself a favor and avoid fitting price action in LLM, it wont give any significant alpha that institutions with way more compute wouldnt have accounted for and captured.
